title: Executable definition of done
description: The `dod[]` slot a refined ticket or prompt envelope may carry. `dod` is EXECUTABLE by construction: every item names the command that proves it, so the engine can report which items are still unproven without asking a human to interpret prose. Prose acceptance criteria stay where they are (`acceptance_criteria`) — this is the machine-checkable subset, not a replacement. The slot is OPTIONAL: a ticket without `dod` behaves exactly as before, which is why the `refine` gate validates the shape only when the key is present. Consumed by `work_engine/directives/backend/refine.ts` (shape gate) and reported by `work_engine/directives/backend/_self_fix.ts` at the PARTIAL exit.

dod.description: May be empty. An empty array means the author declared no machine-checkable done-condition, which is different from omitting the key: omission means the question was never asked. Both are legal and neither blocks.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within the array. Used verbatim in the self-fix PARTIAL exit so a reader can match an unproven item back to the ticket without re-reading the whole envelope.

check.description: The command that proves this item — a test filter, a linter invocation, a curl probe. Prose here defeats the point of the slot: the engine never runs it (the dispatcher spawns no subprocesses, per the delegation contract), it hands it to the agent, and an agent cannot run a sentence.

description.description: Optional human sentence for the halt surface. Absent is fine — `check` is already the falsifiable half.

proven.description: Set by the agent once `check` has actually been run green. Absent or `false` both mean unproven; the engine never infers `true` from a passing suite, because a suite passing is not evidence that THIS check ran.
